name: INA253A2IPWR
title: INA253 (A1, A2, A3): 80 V bidirectional zero-drift current-sense amplifier with built-in 2 mΩ shunt, 100/200/400 mV/A, TSSOP-20
summary: A current monitor with its own 2 mΩ, 0.1 % Kelvin shunt (3 nH) and a chopper-stabilised amplifier in one TSSOP-20. Its inputs work from –4 V to +80 V on either side of the shunt regardless of its 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply, and it measures current in both directions. The output is a voltage set by the fixed transresistance: 100 mV/A (INA253A1), 200 mV/A (INA253A2) or 400 mV/A (INA253A3), around a level the two REF pins set. Input circuitry rejects fast PWM common-mode edges; it carries 15 A continuous up to 85 °C.
key_figures: 2 mΩ, 1.998 to 2.002 mΩ with the amplifier; 3 nH; 4.5 mΩ package

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: High-side current sensing of a solenoid driven by a MOSFET from a rail up to 80 V. The part sits between the switch and the coil, so its inputs swing with the switched node; the coil current returns through the freewheeling diode when the switch opens. REF2 to VS and REF1 to ground put the zero-current output at VS / 2.

circuits.title: Solenoid drive application circuit
circuits.description: Current sensing in the driver of a 12 V, 500 mA hydraulic valve. The INA253A3 (400 mV/A) runs from 5 V with REF1 to ground and REF2 to VS, so the output sits at mid-supply with no current and moves with the coil current in either direction.
notes: The reference pins may instead be joined and driven from a precision reference.

circuits.title: Current sensing in a class-D subsystem
circuits.description: The part sits in series with a speaker on the output of a class-D full bridge, after the left LC filter, to measure the speaker current for diagnostics, coil resistance and impedance. With a 5 V supply, REF1 to ground and REF2 to VS set the zero-current output to 2.5 V; with the 100 mV/A gain a 10 A peak-to-peak current swings the output from 1.5 V to 3.5 V, inside a 5 V ADC range.
notes: Design values: INA253A1 (100 mV/A), 5 V supply, 24 V common-mode, 4 Ω speaker, 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

circuits.title: Ground-referenced output
circuits.description: Unidirectional sensing: both REF pins at ground, so the output sits at ground with no current and rises with current in one direction. Reference connection only: the sense pins are wired straight to the inputs and the current pins are tied together.
notes: IS+ and IS– are joined outside the part, so the shunt carries no current and the output rests at the level the REF pins set.

circuits.title: External reference output
circuits.description: Bidirectional sensing with both REF pins joined and driven from a 2.5 V reference; the zero-current output equals the reference voltage, the most accurate way to set the output level. Reference connection only: the sense pins are wired straight to the inputs and the current pins are tied together.
notes: IS+ and IS– are joined outside the part, so the shunt carries no current and the output rests at the level the REF pins set.

circuits.title: Mid-supply voltage output
circuits.description: Bidirectional sensing with REF2 at VS and REF1 at ground: the zero-current output is VS / 2 and follows the supply. Reference connection only: the sense pins are wired straight to the inputs and the current pins are tied together.
notes: IS+ and IS– are joined outside the part, so the shunt carries no current and the output rests at the level the REF pins set.

circuits.title: Mid-external reference output
circuits.description: REF2 on a 2.5 V reference and REF1 at ground halve the reference: the zero-current output is 1.25 V. Reference connection only: the sense pins are wired straight to the inputs and the current pins are tied together.
notes: IS+ and IS– are joined outside the part, so the shunt carries no current and the output rests at the level the REF pins set.

circuits.title: Setting the reference using a resistor divider
circuits.description: Both REF pins joined and held by a divider from VS for a custom zero-current level. The ADC reads OUT differentially against the divider node, since shifts in the internal impedance disturb a single-ended reading. Reference connection only: the sense pins are wired straight to the inputs and the current pins are tied together.
notes: IS+ and IS– are joined outside the part, so the shunt carries no current and the output rests at the level the REF pins set.

circuits.title: Filter at input pins
circuits.description: An optional RC low-pass between each sense tap and its amplifier input. Each series resistor adds gain error through the input bias currents, so they are kept to 10 Ω or less; the part is accurate without any filter.
notes: IS+ and IS– are joined outside the part.
Gain error from the resistors: see the gain error equations and table.

operation.text: A 2 mΩ, 0.1 % four-wire shunt sits in the package. The load current enters at IS+ and leaves at IS–; SH+ and SH– are its Kelvin taps, which go to IN+ and IN–. The shunt and amplifier are trimmed together, so the system gain figure holds only when the internal amplifier reads the internal shunt; read as a bare resistor through SH+ and SH–, it is about 5 % tolerance.

IS+ to IS– is about 4.5 mΩ in all, of which 2 mΩ is the controlled sense element. Heat in that 4.5 mΩ, not the chip's own supply current, sets how much current the package carries; the limit keeps the resistor and package from damage and the junction at or below 150 °C.

With no air flow and 1 oz copper input planes the part carries 15 A continuous up to 85 °C ambient, derating to 10 A at 125 °C. With air flow and larger 2 oz planes it carries 15 A over the full –40 °C to +125 °C range. Ambient temperature, air flow and board layout all set how well the package sheds heat.
The shunt survives currents above the 15 A continuous limit for short times without harm to the resistor or the amplifier; the short-circuit duration curve gives current against time.

The shunt drifts more from –40 °C to 0 °C than from 0 °C to 125 °C. Self-heating from load current raises the resistor's temperature and moves it out of the colder region where drift is wider. The low drift of shunt and amplifier together keeps the measurement accurate as temperature changes across the specified range.

Circuitry at the input attenuates large common-mode dV/dt steps such as those of PWM motor, solenoid and switching-supply drives. High ac CMRR together with the signal bandwidth keeps output glitches and ringing small without needing a wider amplifier bandwidth.

Bandwidth is the –3 dB bandwidth of the internal amplifier, 350 kHz, fast enough for overcurrent detection. Distortion rises toward the top of the band (THD+N curve), so signals near the bandwidth are measured less accurately while low-frequency signals stay low in distortion.

REF1 and REF2 drive an internal pair of 50 kΩ resistors that set the output's zero-current level; the two pins behave the same. Neither may go below GND or above VS. Unidirectional: both REF pins to ground, and the output rises from ground with current. Bidirectional: both pins joined to a reference voltage (output equals it, the most accurate method), one pin to VS and one to GND (output VS / 2, ratiometric to the supply), or one pin to an external reference and one to ground (output half the reference). The REF pins are meant to be driven from supply, ground or a low-impedance source; a resistor divider on the joined pins works if the output is read differentially against the divider node.
With IN+ above IN– the output rises above its reference level; with IN+ below IN– it falls below it.

No input filter is needed, and the part is most accurate without one. A filter at the output changes the low output impedance the next stage sees. A filter at the inputs uses series resistors at IN+ and IN–; the input bias currents are unequal when a differential voltage is present, so the resistors add a differential error, worse with resistor mismatch. Keep them at 10 Ω or less.

IN+ and IN– work anywhere from –4 V to +80 V whatever VS is, so a 5 V part can sense on an 80 V rail; the output swing stays within the supply. Place a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor close to the VS and GND pins, with more capacitance for a noisy or high-impedance supply. With the output set to mid-supply, supply noise reaches the output, so keep the supply quiet.

With 1 oz copper input planes and no air flow the part is specified to 10 A from –40 °C to +125 °C. Heat leaving the package is the limit: wider, thicker (2 oz) copper and air flow raise it to 15 A over that range; the evaluation module, with 2 oz planes, carries 15 A up to 125 °C. In the layout example the IS pins of each side join a wide plane, the bypass capacitor sits between VS and GND with a via to the supply, and the reserved NC pin (15) and REF1 each have a ground via.

In a PLC remote I/O with one 24 V, 5 A supply feeding eight IO-Link ports of up to 1 A each, the part measures total supply current so a port is enabled only when there is headroom. The current flows one way, so the REF pins go to ground, and the 200 mV/A version fits a 1.8 V ADC range at 9 A.
